To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of deaths in Australia from unintentional drowning is increasing; (2) drowning deaths in Australia are not equally distributed across the country, with a higher number in the Northern Territory and Queensland and a lower number in Tasmania and Victoria; and (3) the drowning rate in Australia is increasing for males aged 25-34 years and decreasing for all other age groups.

(1) there is a need for a comprehensive, evidence-based approach to drowning prevention, (2) the most effective drowning prevention strategies are those that are implemented in a collaborative manner and (3) the best way to achieve collaboration is through the development of partnerships.

the proposition that the most effective way of achieving the goal of drowning prevention is through the development of partnerships and collaboration.
the development and evaluation of partnerships and collaborations to improve drowning prevention.
understanding and improving the effectiveness of partnerships and collaboration for drowning prevention.
